**Architecture-level reconciliation:**
- **Platform scope:** preserve modular Creator Platform direction, but do not interpret “hundreds or thousands of features” as a commitment to implement all of them in 1.0. Current phase/acceptance gates govern execution.
- **Single state/action pipeline:** UI, AI and automation must use one canonical command/action → validation/permission → state/history → renderer → authorized persistence path. No direct D1 writes from browser code and no AI direct DOM/CSS/JS mutation.
- **Data services:** D1 is structured source of truth; R2 is for binary objects, KV/cache/Queues/Durable Objects only when an explicit workload contract, binding, ownership and failure behavior are defined. Historical architecture text does not prove those services are currently configured.
- **Identity domains:** site/page/section/container/component/element/media/schedule/action/version/audit/task/automation/agent/template/token/data-source IDs must remain semantically distinct and scoped. A generic stable-ID requirement does not itself define uniqueness, foreign keys, retention or authorization.
- **AI and automation:** intent/plan/validate/preview/approve/execute/verify/audit is the future safe path. Human editing must remain fully usable without AI; autonomy, specialist agents and stream intelligence are deferred until permission, evaluation, observability, cost, privacy and rollback contracts are approved.
- **Streamer/content scope:** live state, schedule, VOD, Shorts/Clips, community metrics, sponsor/press, campaigns and content calendar are preserved as roadmap requirements. Each provider/API, content ingestion, publishing and analytics capability needs its own permission, rate-limit, stale-data and partial-failure contract.
- **Testing:** unit/integration/API/D1-R2-KV/E2E/smoke/visual/responsive/accessibility/security/performance/backup-restore/migration/concurrency/AI rollback/production deployment are distinct test classes; none is proven by a generic “tests passed” statement.

**Status:** 42 source bullets individually keyed UPD-001–UPD-042. Architecture constraints are retained; candidate mapping and phase/owner/dependency/DoD/test/acceptance remain OPEN. P0.2 **IN PROGRESS / NOT PASS**. Documentation-only; no runtime code/data changed and no tests were run.

### 41.3.46. P0.2 — AI safety crosswalk completeness and memory/evaluation boundary (2026-10-13)

**Confirmed registry comparison:**
- F.8-04 now explicitly includes AI-004 context/privacy filtering, AI-018 prompt-injection/untrusted-content tests, AI-019 human approval and AI-020 AI-free fallback, along with canonical Editor actions and server-side permissions. This is a mapping correction only; all controls remain deferred until a phase-specific security acceptance is passed.
- F.8-08 retains the human-reviewed clip/export and AI Control Center scope. AI-018/019/020 remain distinct controls and cannot be collapsed into a generic “AI safety” checkbox.

**Still-open semantic exception:**
- F.8-07 groups live/silence/speech/chat/audio/OBS/highlights/VOD/clips/feedback/opt-in memory under AI-014–016. The registry defines AI-014 as transcript/chapter/highlight/clip candidates, AI-015 as stream diagnostics/summary, and AI-016 as specialist-agent roles. None alone proves streamer profile, long-term memory, preference management, evaluation history or feedback governance.
- Keep F.8-07 as a high-level roadmap umbrella, but its implementation must be split into separate scoped capabilities before the 3.0–8.0 phases: (a) provider/source and live-monitoring capability; (b) transcript/clip generation; (c) opt-in profile/memory with retention/export/delete/consent; (d) evaluation/outcome/experiment tracking; (e) human-reviewed feedback/opt-out. Do not invent new stable IDs until the full 359-ID bidirectional reconciliation determines whether existing AI-004/010/012/015/016/017 and SEC-011/ANL IDs can cover the exact contract.
- Acceptance must include provider unavailability/stale data, no microphone/chat ingestion without explicit permission/consent, memory opt-out/delete, prompt injection, false-positive handling, evaluation reproducibility, audit, rollback and an AI-free manual workflow.

**Status:** F.8-04/08 mapping completeness improved; F.8-07 remains **OPEN / PARTIAL**. P0.2 **IN PROGRESS / NOT PASS**. Documentation-only; no runtime code/data changed and no tests were run.

**Precedence and semantic controls:**
- MASTER-2.75 stage order is historical only. Do not reactivate its stage sequence or treat old checkmarks as current completion.
- MASTER-2.76's AI-free product definition is preserved as a product invariant: core website/editor/media/publish/stream/schedule/content/community/business/backup workflows must remain usable without AI.
- The AI orchestrator, agent registry, context/memory, learning and clip-generation capabilities remain optional later-phase work. Deterministic APIs, permissions, preview, audit and rollback must exist first.
- Cross-domain security, privacy, accessibility, ownership, backup/recovery and testing are baseline constraints for every phase, not an end-stage feature.
- Stage headings and repeated capability statements are not separate new features by themselves; retain their source keys and merge only with explicit scope/acceptance comparison.
- No runtime code/data changed; no tests run.

**Status:** 468 historical source rows keyed; current canonical mapping, duplicate/reinforcement decisions, owner/phase/dependency and acceptance remain OPEN. P0.2 **IN PROGRESS / NOT PASS**.

### 41.3.59. P0.2 — HIST-001–HIST-140 mapping integrity and first semantic repairs (2026-10-13)

**Source checked:** current §24 canonical feature-ID registry and the §41.3.58 historical 01–140 matrix in this same MASTER. The audit used the current branch's complete MASTER blob, not a partial line fetch.

**Structural result:** §24 contains 359 feature-ID entries and 359 unique IDs. The historical matrix contains 140 unique HIST rows; all 140 rows have a non-empty candidate mapping, and every explicit PREFIX-NNN token extracted from those candidate columns resolves to an ID in §24. This proves structural referential integrity only. It does **not** prove that a candidate mapping is semantically correct, that every source item is cross-linked to C.23/F/H/roadmap rows, or that owner/phase/dependency/DoD/test/acceptance has been verified.

**Direct semantic defects found and repaired in the canonical matrix:**
- HIST-030 (“Responsive engine foundation”) previously pointed to EDT-035/036 (mobile action bar and mobile panel switching), which do not own the responsive engine contract. The row now points to EDT-024/025/026 (responsive override/inheritance/reset, viewport preview, and visibility/order/column behavior), DSN-006 (breakpoint tokens), and QA-002/004/005 for data/editor/browser/accessibility verification. These are candidate owner links; acceptance remains open.
- HIST-041 (“Canvas zoom / fit / grid / viewport UX”) previously included EDT-016 (layout container/stack/row/columns/grid elements) as a proxy for canvas grid behavior. The row now separates EDT-007 (canvas viewport/zoom/pan/fit) and EDT-010 (alignment guides/snap/grid), with QA-004/005. Browser/device acceptance remains open.

**Remaining limitation:** all 140 decisions still require row-by-row semantic acceptance, exact source-key links, canonical owner and surface confirmation, current phase/dependency, measurable DoD, positive and negative tests, and acceptance evidence. Broad historical rows (for example “Security hardening”, “Regression tests”, and grouped platform names) must be decomposed into their constituent requirements where their source wording contains multiple independent acceptance obligations. Do not treat a valid ID as proof that the ID covers the whole historical requirement.

**Status:** two concrete semantic mapping defects corrected; structural check passed; historical matrix remains **OPEN / PARTIAL** and P0.2 remains **IN PROGRESS / NOT PASS**. Documentation-only; no runtime code, database, Worker configuration, or tests changed.

### 41.3.61. P0.2 — Editor command, node-binding and element-capability semantic pass (2026-10-13)

**Scope:** targeted review of historical rows HIST-025–HIST-053 against the §24 Editor contracts. This pass corrects candidate mappings that pointed to adjacent but semantically different controls or block families.

**Canonical rows corrected:**
- `HIST-025` adds `EDT-003` for the command mutation pipeline; transaction/history/action-registry IDs alone did not explicitly name the core mutation contract.
- `HIST-027` replaces drag/drop and library-search proxies with `EDT-003/004/005/011` for mutation, transaction, history and element lifecycle operations.

- `HIST-034` narrows Geometry Inspector to geometry constraints, Property Registry/schema, resolved viewport value and responsive override (`EDT-009/021/022/023/024`); preview and visibility/order behavior remain separately tracked.
- `HIST-036` adds the reorder/reparent contract (`EDT-011`) to drag/drop and geometry, and removes layout block capability as a proxy.
- `HIST-040` explicitly maps multi-select to `EDT-038` and removes layer lock/hide/rename as a substitute for group/ungroup.
- `HIST-052` no longer maps rich text to table/accordion/tabs/form (`EDT-019`). The baseline text block maps to `EDT-017`; rich-text formatting, schema, safe paste and save/reload still need an explicit owner and acceptance contract.
- `HIST-053` maps image/video/embed to `EDT-018` and removes unrelated table/form capability `EDT-019`; media storage, upload validation, SVG safety, authorized download and safe embed remain separate acceptance requirements.

**Crosswalk validation:** current §24 registry remains 359 unique IDs; HIST matrix remains 140 unique rows. A full expansion pass over slash-compressed IDs and numeric ranges found zero references to IDs absent from §24 after the SEO range correction in §41.3.60. This is structural only and does not close semantic coverage.

**Status:** eight canonical historical rows corrected in this pass. P0.2 remains **IN PROGRESS / NOT PASS**; historical-source links, owner/phase/dependency, measurable DoD, positive/negative tests and acceptance evidence remain open. **Validation:** §24 still has 359 unique stable IDs; §41.3.58 still has 140 historical rows. Expanded validation of numeric ranges and slash-compressed references reports zero unknown IDs. This validates only the crosswalk's ID references, not implementation or semantic closure.

**Status:** eight historical rows corrected in this pass. P0.2 remains **IN PROGRESS / NOT PASS**; full row-by-row owner/phase/dependency/DoD/test/acceptance and bidirectional source links remain open. Documentation-only; no runtime code/data/configuration changed and no tests were run.

### 41.3.81. P0.2 — MASTER-1.2 page-lock owner/phase disposition and concurrency boundary (2026-10-14)

**Source:** `MASTER-1.2-VISUAL-EDITOR-SPEC.md`, source key `M12-L0040` (“oldalzárolás”); related historical source key `H34.08` and canonical registry definitions in §24.

**Finding:** the source phrase “oldalzárolás” is too short to prove whether it means (a) an edit lease/lock on the whole page, (b) a UI layer lock, or (c) an exclusive lock used to prevent simultaneous editing by multiple users. These are not interchangeable. `EDT-014` covers element/layer lock behavior; `EDT-029` covers revision-conflict recovery. Neither proves a page-level collaboration lease. `TEAM-004` is approval/review/activity feed, not live collaborative editing or lock ownership.

**Disposition:**
- **KEEP / DEFER from 1.0 core:** retain page-level editing lock as a distinct future collaboration/concurrency capability under §39.6 (4.0 — multi-creator, teams, collaboration and SaaS readiness). It must not block the current single-creator Editor slice unless implementation evidence reveals an existing mandatory safety dependency.
- **Do not merge it into layer lock or revision conflict recovery.** Those capabilities remain independently required.
- **Provisional owner:** future TEAM/concurrency domain. `TEAM-007` is a *candidate only*, not yet a stable registry ID; no new stable ID is minted before the P0.2 bidirectional registry reconciliation is closed. At P0.2 closure, check the complete §24 registry for a true existing equivalent; if none exists, create one stable ID and update the registry plus every source crosswalk atomically.
- **H34.08 disposition:** PARTIAL mapping only. `TEAM-004` and `EDT-029` may remain as related review/conflict references but do not close the historical collaboration/concurrency requirement. The future TEAM/concurrency owner must explicitly cover concurrent edit leases, lock acquire/renew/release/expiry, stale-owner recovery, unauthorized lock bypass, conflict UX and multi-tab/multi-user negative tests where the product scope requires them.
- **P0.2 closure condition:** the source item is now assigned a non-ambiguous disposition and target phase; the stable-ID decision remains gated on the final registry-wide duplicate check. The H34.08 crosswalk must be updated to mark this phase boundary rather than implying current implementation.

**Evidence boundary:** this is a documentation/semantic decision from the source wording and existing registry/roadmap definitions. It does not assert that page locks, concurrent editing, presence or collaboration are implemented. No runtime code, schema or provider configuration is changed by this entry.
